name: ossify
description: Skeleton-first lifecycle from Release 0 through MVP and v1. An alternate replacement for scaffold-onboard + scaffold-dev, not a stage alongside them. workspace-init is optional - /ossify:start and /ossify:adopt author the topology declaration themselves. Since 1.8.0 /ossify:run-spine accepts an optional --external-executor flag handing the work items of a round to a caller-supplied, provider-neutral in-session procedure; the no-flag command is unchanged.

interface.shortDescription: Plan a release as a skeleton and drive it from Release 0 through MVP and v1.
interface.longDescription: Ossify plans a release as a skeleton, drives its spine round by round, and closes it with a ceremony that harvests what the round learned. It replaces the scaffold-onboard + scaffold-dev pair rather than composing with them — install one lifecycle or the other, not both. workspace-init is optional as of 1.3.0: the first entry point authors .ossify/topology.json itself when nothing resolves on the walk-up path, and reads a workspace-init .workspace/pairing.json as a translated fallback when one exists. The grill and the adversarial critic are internal (the challenge skill) since 1.1.0, so the release-planning veto and the spine-close audit run on every install; an external fresh-frame adversary joins close-depth audits when one is configured. One limit on Codex specifically: round execution dispatches an implementer subagent that only the Claude Code and OpenCode surfaces register.
defaultPrompt: Onboard this project's spec core with ossify.
Open the next release and plan its spine.
